Really good. And the methods they used weren't really good, but the basic principles of recording the holograms on photoresist were perfectly good. They just needed some refinement. So that's what I did. I always thought that the holograms that came out of Light Impressions were beautiful. Well, thank you. But I would say that the crispness and the brightness of the holograms came from two things. One was the particular 2D, 3D techniques. We used. Gives you sharp edges. And it's still the best there is using those contact masks. The other is we had a company culture of don't send it out unless it's as good as we can get it. And we threw away a lot of hologram masters because of that. But I think it paid off. You know, a lot of people collect those type of holograms now. I remember the test he did that really proved it was working. It was the end of a tree branch that had twigs going in all directions. The whole image was about a foot deep. color components to superimpose through that whole volume.
